MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Larger breadboards fit my existing mini boards, PCB supplies, and jumper wires because they give me more room to assemble circuits.",
    "The Arduino sensor and test leads feel useful alongside my prototyping supplies: one offers a plausible project component, while the other helps hold connections during testing."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The 12V relay looks related to my earlier relay purchase, but my previous module used 5V; a different voltage is not automatically useful for the same project.",
    "The thermal camera shares a temperature-measurement purpose with my infrared thermometer, but I have no current need for imaging beyond the checks my thermometer handles.",
    "Magnesium ribbon, printer filament, conductive paint, and specialized glue require projects I have not indicated, while 55 pounds of silica gel exceeds any current need."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My purchases seem to have been read as interest in almost any workshop or experimental supply, although I choose items for specific practical uses.",
    "Similar product names or functions seem to count too heavily when voltage, quantity, and whether I need another tool can change my decision."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Compatibility with my existing electronics supplies matters, especially operating voltage and how a component connects to the boards and wires I already use.",
    "I am more interested in useful additions to my current setup than supplies that assume I have started chemistry, 3D printing, or conductive-paint projects.",
    "My purchases span several years, so an older purchase alone does not mean I currently need a replacement or a more specialized version."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognize my electronics prototyping interests but stretch them into specialized tools and unrelated projects without enough evidence of a current need."
}
